problems.memo_sentence: "The paper reports that QSVM improves classification accuracy by up to about 20% and reduces training time by around 50%, including 92.3% accuracy on S&P 500 anomaly detection and detection of 95% of anomalies in their summary."
problems.source_evidence: The paper’s results section says: "Table 2 & figure 3 shows the performance comparison of QSVM... QSVM outperforms the classical models on all the datasets and assures 92.3% classification accuracy on S&P 500 market anomaly detection" and earlier in the review it says "works like [1], [3], and [12] show how the QSVM and hybrid quantum-classical models outperform their classical variants..."
problems.explanation: The memo presents the 92.3% accuracy and 50% training-time reduction as the paper’s own reported experimental result, but the paper frames these as comparisons to cited works and a review of existing studies. The paper does not clearly claim it independently achieved 95% anomaly detection in its own experiments.

problems.memo_sentence: "QAOA is claimed to improve portfolio optimization with a 10–15% Sharpe ratio uplift and 25% faster optimization, including a reported Sharpe ratio of 1.45 for a 50‑asset portfolio and an example allocation of 45% equities and 30% bonds."
problems.source_evidence: The paper states: "QAOA has shown an improvement in the Sharpe ratio by about 10-15%, and it also converges to an optimum solution 25% quicker compared to the classical methods" and Table 4 reports Sharpe ratios for datasets/portfolios, but nowhere gives an example allocation of 45% equities and 30% bonds.
problems.explanation: The memo adds a specific portfolio allocation example that is not in the source text. It also treats the Sharpe-ratio figures as if they were the paper’s own experimental outputs, whereas the paper presents them as comparative results against cited methods.

problems.memo_sentence: "QPCA is reported to reduce dimensionality by ~90% while preserving around 95% variance (e.g., 95.2% variance retained on S&P 500 indicators)..."
problems.source_evidence: The paper says in the abstract and results: "QPCA is then applied to reduce the dimensions of the data while preserving 95% of the variance in the data and decreasing the data dimensionality by 90%" and Table 5 compares QPCA against methods [5], [9], and [18].
problems.explanation: The memo attributes the 95.2% variance-retention figure to the paper’s own QPCA result, but the paper presents it as a benchmarked comparison against cited methods. This is a citation-attribution issue rather than a direct experimental claim by the authors.

problems.memo_sentence: "QBM is said to increase forecasting accuracy by about 5–10% with 30% faster convergence, achieving roughly 88–88.5% stock‑price prediction accuracy."
problems.source_evidence: The paper states: "Financial time series prediction will be done using QBM, which can yield an increase of up to 5-10% in the accuracy of the prediction and 30% faster convergence" and Table 6 reports 87.5% stock-price prediction accuracy, compared with cited methods [5], [9], and [18].
problems.explanation: The memo rounds and reframes the table values as the paper’s own achieved accuracy, but the source presents them as comparative results against prior methods. The memo also shifts the exact reported 87.5% to an approximate 88–88.5%.

problems.memo_sentence: "For security, lattice‑based cryptography is claimed to provide 99.9% security against classical and quantum attacks with roughly 10–15% extra execution time, yet still securing financial transactions with minimal overhead in their examples."
problems.source_evidence: The paper says: "Encryption algorithms maintain 99.9% security certainty against quantum decryption attempts" and "a 10-15% increase in computational overhead against the similar settings of a classical cryptographic method like RSA"; Table 7 compares encryption/decryption times against methods [5], [9], and [18].
problems.explanation: The memo turns the paper’s comparative benchmark into a direct claim of the authors’ own achieved security and overhead. The source frames these as literature-review findings and benchmark comparisons, not a validated security guarantee from the authors’ implementation.

problems.memo_sentence: "The paper acknowledges several technical and organizational limitations. On the quantum side, it notes that current hardware noise and limited qubit coherence can seriously affect the performance and reliability of QSVM, QAOA, QPCA, and QBM, and that scalability to larger datasets remains unresolved because performance may degrade as data size and complexity grow."
problems.source_evidence: The source also explicitly states: "the real-world quantum hardware is not yet ready to support this kind of large-scale computation needed by many financial applications" and "the scalability of the quantum algorithms is still an open question, since many papers mention that while the quantum models perform better than classical on small to medium-sized datasets, their performance may degrade when the size and complexity of the dataset are scaling up in the process."
problems.explanation: The memo captures the general idea but omits the stronger limitation that real-world quantum hardware is not yet ready for the large-scale computations needed in finance. That omission matters because it is a central caveat in the review section.
